chapter: Moten band, arranging and the guitar
title: How Basie became Count
summary: Moten kept saying Basie was no account for leaving arrangements unfinished, so Durham wrote a tune called The Count.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: The story about that -- Benny Morton used to say, oh,

that guy ain't no 'count. You know, that's a ____. So I wrote that tune and gave it to Benny to play. And we'd say, play the Count, Benny. Everybody would laugh, you know? Basie didn't know what it was all about, that Benny wasn't -- and, like, he had kept saying, Basie wasn't no 'count. So I wrote a tune called The Count (inaudible). See, but we just called it the Count. That's how he got his title.
That's how he got that title. Now, --
I mean, who said Basie was no account?

Because he'd say, Basie, play this for me. Man, I can't read that. Oh, and he'd say, you're going to bring up something now, you're supposed to be an arranger. Sometimes Basie used to help him with the arranging. I'd say, Basie, set down and make up something, because he'd make up a little something, I'd write it down. I'd say, man, you've got terrific ideas, but he wouldn't stick with it. He'd get up, finish it, Alan, finish it, Alan. And that's all he'd want to do. He'd say, now, I'll take this one, Benny. And he'd sit down and play that little part and a little bit more and then he'd get up and he's gone. Benny -- where is that guy, he ain't no account. And that was the expression always. So that's why I named that tune The Count.
